title: Classify quantized attention scales separately from moe_scales (SCHEMA_VERSION 3)
description:
Found during the gh-30 bot-review backfill audit (iz3.6 / PR #20, thread from codeant-ai). PR #20 added rank-2 int8 attention classification for QuantWeight tensors but never gave their paired QuantScales tensors a matching path.

On main, src/inventory/mod.rs classification rule 2 is unconditional:
  (TensorRole::QuantScales, TensorDType::F32, _) => TensorKind::MoeScales
No AttnScales/QuantizedAttentionScales variant exists anywhere (git grep MoeScales -- src/ finds only the MoE label). docs/tensor-schema.md:115 documents the same unconditional rule.

Impact on the shipped Grok-1 ckpt-0 map is currently nil — the f32 scales half lives inside the int8 shard bodies there. The defect bites any checkpoint layout that exposes scales as their own top-level record: attention quantization scales get counted as MoE scales, skewing moe_scales totals, block summaries, expert-atlas views, and SAAQ region classification.
design:
classify_tensor (src/inventory/mod.rs:249) currently sees one RawTensor; the caller loop at :105-106 already holds the whole raws slice for the shard. Pass the paired weight's rank (or the preceding QuantWeight tensor) and return MoeScales only when the pair's weight is rank-3; emit an attention-scales kind for a rank-2 int8 partner.

Adding a TensorKind variant is an export-surface change, so it must ship with inventory::SCHEMA_VERSION 2 -> 3 plus updates to docs/tensor-schema.md, docs/export-contracts.md, and CHANGELOG.md.

Rejected alternative: keep MoeScales for rank-3-paired scales and fall through to Unknown { reason } otherwise. That trips the unknown_tensors == 0 coverage gate on any checkpoint that does expose such scales, so the new-variant route is safer.
acceptance_criteria: Paired rank-2 int8 scales classify as attention scales, not MoeScales; SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 2->3; tensor-schema.md, export-contracts.md and CHANGELOG.md updated; regression test covers a rank-2-paired scales tensor; cargo test --locked green
notes: Effort: medium. Source: audit report pr-20.md gap G20.1. Deliberately excluded from the gh-30 audit follow-up PR because the schema bump is a breaking export-contract change that grok-ozempic consumes. The originating PR #20 thread must stay UNRESOLVED until this lands on main (per docs/contributing-bot-reviews.md: fixed-now/gap never resolves early).

title: Restore dependency vulnerability scanning (cargo-audit) in CI
description:
PR #35 (closed, never merged) carried three pillars: clippy, non-blocking Qodana, and a cargo-audit security job. PR #48 rebuilt the first two as jobs inside .github/workflows/ci.yml but did NOT carry over dependency scanning. Found during the gh-30 bot-review backfill audit (iz3.8 / PR #35).

Confirmed absent on main: no cargo-audit, no cargo-deny, no deny.toml/audit.toml, no .github/dependabot.yml. Four of PR #35's nine bot threads (T2, T4, T6, T7) are classified deferred ONLY because this surface vanished, so their lessons are unapplied rather than wrong.
design: Add one cargo-audit job to ci.yml that re-applies all four bot lessons at once: pinned taiki-e/install-action (or 'cargo install cargo-audit --locked') for a reproducible install; step-level continue-on-error: true so it advises without gating the #33 required check; 'set -euo pipefail' before any tee so the audit exit status is not masked; and 'if: always()' on the log upload so the report survives exactly the run that finds vulnerabilities.
acceptance_criteria: ci.yml has an advisory cargo-audit job; install is --locked or SHA-pinned; pipefail set before tee; upload runs on failure; rust-ci remains the only required gate
notes: Effort: small. Source: audit report pr-35.md note 2. Related borderline nit: docs/ci.md:137 tells contributors 'cargo install cargo-llvm-cov' without --locked (local-dev snippet, not CI, so not the same defect).
